questions.q: What is the Regional Manager's actual question, from Lesson 1?
options: How are my stores doing, day to day
Should the pipeline move to Import or DirectQuery
Are the two Gold tables still reconciling correctly
Which categories are driving sales, and whether that differs store to store
questions.explain: The Regional Manager's ask is a composition question about which categories drive sales and whether that varies by store -- not a time-trend question.

questions.q: Why can't gold.daily_sales_summary answer the Regional Manager's question?
options: It only contains data for a single store
It does not contain a store_id column
It has no category dimension at all -- it was deliberately built at the store/day grain only
It is stored in Bronze, not Gold
questions.explain: gold.daily_sales_summary was built without a category breakdown, so it structurally cannot answer a question about category composition -- that's what gold.category_breakdown is for.

questions.q: Why does this page use a bar chart of total_sales by category instead of a line chart?
options: Bar charts are required whenever a Gold table has a quantity column
The question is about comparing discrete categories against each other, not about a trend over time
Power BI cannot plot a category field on a line chart
A line chart would require DirectQuery mode
questions.explain: Bars make a side-by-side comparison across a handful of categories easy to read; a line chart is built for trend-over-time questions, which this one isn't.

questions.q: Why is sale_date a slicer on this page instead of the chart's main axis, unlike on the Store Ops page?
options: DirectQuery mode disables date fields as chart axes
This page's question is about category composition, not about a trend over time, so date becomes a filter rather than the chart's subject
Slicers are mandatory on every Power BI page regardless of the question
gold.category_breakdown does not actually contain a sale_date column
questions.explain: Whatever dimension a question is actually about becomes the chart's main axis; whatever dimension is used to focus the view becomes a slicer. Here that's category as axis, date as slicer.

questions.q: Why does this page include a store_id slicer, just like the Store Ops page?
options: Because store_id is the chart's main axis on this page
The Regional Manager's question explicitly asks whether the category mix differs store to store
Because gold.category_breakdown is physically partitioned by store_id
Because Power BI requires every page in a shared model to use identical slicers
questions.explain: The Lesson 1 ask explicitly includes checking whether the category breakdown differs store to store, so a store_id slicer lets the same bar chart answer that for any store or group of stores.
